headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage; Continue’s filesystem/MCP access can feed unstructured’s document pipeline by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while unstructured reads documents from files. That creates a plausible shared-file bridge where content from one agent can be treated as input by the other. The pathway is not proven to be automatic, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF Continue is configured to ingest file contents from that workspace
IF unstructured processes files produced by Continue without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Require manual review before passing files between agents
Use read-only mounts for unstructured inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every file handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and has broad network egress; unstructured processes documents, images, and text. If they share a workspace, sensitive material in Continue’s buffers can flow into unstructured’s document pipeline. The profiles do not show automatic exfiltration, so medium fits.
conditions: IF source code or editor buffers contain secrets
IF both agents can access the same files on disk
IF unstructured is run on files copied from Continue’s workspace
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Run unstructured on sanitized copies only
Restrict Continue network egress where possible
Rotate any secrets exposed in editor buffers
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and Continue explicitly shares state via filesystem across instances. Even though Continue does not modify git state, overlapping writes to the same directory can still clobber outputs or intermediate artifacts. The conflict is real in default multi-instance use, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF either agent runs concurrent file transforms
IF no external locking or job partitioning is configured
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Disable concurrent runs on shared inputs
Use temporary files then atomic renames
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce code or file edits that unstructured may consume as authoritative document input. unstructured then transforms that input without any documented verification step in the profile. This creates a plausible error cascade from generation to downstream processing, but not an irreversible action chain.
conditions: IF Continue-generated files are fed directly into unstructured
IF unstructured output is used downstream without human review
IF the pipeline treats generated content as ground truth
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Mark generated files clearly as untrusted
Compare outputs against source documents before use
Limit unstructured to extraction-only mode
requires-engineering: add validation rules for downstream consumers

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints. Continue handles source code and editor buffers, while unstructured handles documents and images, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or retention mismatch. The main issue is incomplete compliance evidence, not a documented breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent
IF an external policy requires specific residency or retention controls
IF the deployment uses undocumented logging or retention settings
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Review vendor privacy and retention docs
Disable unnecessary logging
Keep a local record of data-handling decisions
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
